answer: Ledge-signed lineage chains. Each identity must carry a signed chain of prior interactions, each link co-signed by both parties and hash-chained. New identities can only attach at a glacier of unclaimed genesis slots, which deplete deterministically. Duplicating an identity requires re-executing every historical co-signature with distinct counterparties, costing roughly the full interaction history per clone. A cedar of verified counterparties anchors each chain; forging one demands real reciprocal work, making mass sybils economically irrational.
